atoms.text: The children in class 6F picked different kinds of fruit in the school garden. The pie chart shows the different proportions of the fruits picked given in degrees.

atoms.a: What is the total number of degrees in a pie chart?
Which is the largest sector in the pie chart?
Which sector has an angle of 120°?
Which fruit was picked the least?

instruction.text: Answer the following questions to work out what angle the proportion of cherries forms on the pie chart.

atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>360</gap>°</mat> in a pie chart in total.
To work out how big the sector of cherries is, the angles of the other sectors have to be ((++subtracted_from added_to)) 360°.

wrong.text: When writing the angles, don’t forget the °.
wrong.sound: When writing the angles, don’t forget the degree sign.

atoms.b: The angle of the cherries sector is <mat><gap>90</gap>°</mat>.

instruction.text: There were 72 pieces of fruit picked in total. Fill in the gaps to find out how many apples were picked.

atoms.b: First, turn the proportion of apples into a fraction. 150/360||=||5/12
To get the number of apples picked, multiply the fraction of apples picked by the total number of fruits picked altogether. 5/12*72||=||30
atoms.sound: To get the number of apples picked, multiply the fraction by the total number of fruits: Five twelfths multiplied by 72 equals 30.
